description.t: This course continues the study of programming using the Java language, with emphasis on object-oriented design. Students learn to model problems with classes, inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces, to handle errors, to store data in collections and files, and to test their programs. Throughout the term they practice working in teams and taking responsibility for the quality and honesty of their software, culminating in a team mini-project.

clos.title: Object-oriented concepts
clos.statement: Design, implement and defend an original, scalable distributed system architecture for an enterprise setting.

clos.title: Object-oriented problem solving
clos.statement: List the names of the primitive data types of Java.

clos.title: Responsible teamwork
clos.statement: Compute the time complexity of common sorting algorithms using Big-O notation.

ilos.text: Describe the purpose of a class and an object in a Java program

plan.contents: Course orientation; review of Java syntax; classes and objects
plan.activities: Lecture-discussion on classes and objects; guided coding of a Student class
plan.tasks: - Seatwork: identify the classes and objects in a short problem description

ilos.text: Explain how encapsulation protects the data of an object

plan.contents: Encapsulation: access modifiers, constructors, getters and setters
plan.activities: Live coding of an Account class with private fields; pair debugging exercise

ilos.text: Describe how a subclass inherits and overrides the members of a superclass

plan.contents: Inheritance, the super keyword and method overriding
plan.activities: Demonstration of a Vehicle class hierarchy; drawing class diagrams in groups
plan.tasks: - Seatwork: draw a class diagram for a given inheritance problem

ilos.text: Apply polymorphism to write code that handles different subclasses through one superclass type

plan.activities: Laboratory: implement a Shape hierarchy with an abstract class and an overridden area method

ilos.text: Implement an interface in a class to satisfy a defined contract

plan.contents: Interfaces and their use as contracts
plan.activities: Laboratory: implement a Payable interface in several Employee classes

ilos.text: Organize classes into packages and justify a design using cohesion and coupling

plan.contents: Packages, access control and design principles: cohesion and coupling
plan.activities: Group refactoring workshop on a poorly organized program

ilos.text: Design the classes of a mini-project by applying object-oriented principles

plan.contents: Review of object-oriented design; specification of the mini-project
plan.activities: Design clinic: each team presents its class design and receives feedback
plan.tasks: - Class design submission for the mini-project

ilos.text: Write code that handles runtime errors with exceptions

plan.contents: Exception handling: try, catch, finally and custom exceptions
plan.activities: Laboratory: add input validation and exception handling to a banking program

ilos.text: Use collections to store and process groups of objects

plan.contents: The collections framework: lists, sets and maps
plan.activities: Laboratory: build a student record manager with ArrayList and HashMap

ilos.text: Sort collections of objects using Comparable and Comparator

plan.contents: Generics and sorting with Comparable and Comparator
plan.activities: Laboratory: sort student records by grade and by name

ilos.text: Read and write data in text files from a Java program

plan.contents: File input and output: reading and writing text files
plan.activities: Laboratory: save and load the student record manager from a file

ilos.text: Create unit tests that verify the behavior of classes

plan.contents: Unit testing with JUnit and debugging practices
plan.activities: Pair programming: write tests for the record manager, then fix the defects they reveal

ilos.text: Collaborate with teammates using version control and code review

plan.contents: Teamwork in software development: version control and code review
plan.activities: Team workshop on a shared repository; peer code review with a checklist

ilos.text: Explain how documentation and respect for users' data reflect responsible programming

plan.contents: Responsible software practice: documentation, licensing and user privacy
plan.activities: Case discussion of privacy mistakes in real applications; documentation workshop

ilos.text: Present and demonstrate a team application, stating honestly what it can and cannot do

plan.activities: Team project demonstrations with a question-and-answer round
plan.tasks: - Mini-project demonstration with a rubric-based evaluation
